zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Falaq
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ أعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الفَلَقِ﴾ ("Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak"): it is the falaq of the morning, i.e. its light; one also says ”فَرَقُ الصُّبْحِ“, and one says ”هُوَ أبْيَنُ مِن فَلَقِ الصُّبْحِ“ ("it is clearer than the break of morning"). And the meaning of ”اَلْفَلْقُ“ is creation. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فالِقُ الإصْباحِ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 96] ("the Cleaver of daybreak") and ﴿فالِقُ الحَبِّ والنَّوى﴾ [al-Anʿām: 95] ("the Cleaver of grain and date-stone"). Likewise He cleaves the earth with vegetation and the clouds with rain. If you reflect on creation, it becomes clear to you that most of His creating is through cleaving open; so al-falaq is all created things, and the break of morning is part of that.

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿وَمِن شَرِّ غاسِقٍ إذا وقَبَ﴾ ("and from the evil of darkness when it settles"): by ”غاسِقٍ“ the night is meant. ﴿إذا وقَبَ﴾: when it enters. The night was called ”غاسِقٌ“ — and Allah knows best — because it is colder than the day, and ”اَلْغاسِقُ“ is the cold.

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿وَمِن شَرِّ النَّفّاثاتِ في العُقَدِ﴾ ("and from the evil of the blowers on knots"): ”اَلنَّفّاثاتُ“ are the sorceresses; they blow (tanfuthu), i.e. they spit without saliva, as if it were blowing, as everyone who performs incantations does.
